fieldsRead.text: The Dutch-taught Algemene Cultuurwetenschappen route studies visual art, literature, music, film, television and performance through historical, theoretical and social perspectives. Students develop cultural criticism, research and cultural-sector practice.

Three UCR programmes offer related routes through arts and media, culture and power, or literature and communication. Radboud provides more dedicated music and performance study, festival production and a separate bachelor thesis. The comparison uses Radboud’s currently published indicative plan for students starting in 2027.

Radboud describes these 2027–2030 course offerings as indicative and subject to change. This planning comparison does not guarantee future courses or replace the applicable programme regulations. Mentoring/PPO and RADAr academic Dutch are zero-credit requirements.
Mentoring/PPO and RADAr academic-language requirements carry 0 EC and are recorded separately from the 180 EC credit total.
Two 15 EC Faculty of Arts minors, one in each second-year semester. Specific examples are indicative rather than guaranteed future offerings.

The UCR programmes offer substantial art history, literature, film, media and cultural interpretation. Radboud also requires music analysis, opera and musical theatre, performance culture, festival work and a separate bachelor thesis. UCR does not reproduce these specialist sequences. Its creative laboratory centres poetic and hybrid projects; its historical seminar develops research concerning the American Century.

A broad arts-and-culture route combining art history and heritage, literature, film and media with stylistics, social theory, ethics and qualitative inquiry. Historiography examines how art is interpreted; the historical research seminar develops source-based inquiry concerning the American Century rather than a dedicated cultural-studies thesis.

A cultural-studies route examining identity and power through art, literature, media, gender history and heritage. Political philosophy, social theory, empire, social movements and conflict provide specific contexts; qualitative inquiry and an American-history research seminar develop complementary methods.

A literature, film and communication route organised around close reading, adaptation, documentary, rhetoric, stylistics and creative communication. Art history and material culture provide selected cultural contexts; general philosophy, ethics and qualitative methods contribute complementary analytical tools.

finding: Every selected reader field and description was read against the sources/current workbook. No old military-history claim, unverified Vasari detail or categorical music exclusion remains. Partial literary-power relationship states the direct critical-reading overlap and different scope. Important music, performance, festival and dedicated thesis gaps are explicit. Current external intake is clearly indicative, with separate zero-credit obligations and genuine choice space. No app code change, local R/Shiny/browser, screenshots or live modals; actual representative rendering remains a final-release requirement.
